summary: Count to 100 by ones and tens, and count on from any number up to 100.
Count up to 20 objects one by one; the last number said tells how many.
Name the position of objects in a line with ordinal words such as first, second, third.
Recognize how many items (0 to 10) are in a small set at a glance, without counting.
Read, write and show whole numbers from 0 to 20.
Show numbers up to 20 as a ten and some ones using objects or drawings.
Compare two groups of up to 10 objects by matching or counting: more, fewer or equal.
Compare two whole numbers using the words greater than, less than or equal.
Show adding and taking away within 10 with objects, fingers, drawings, sounds or acting out.
Break numbers up to 10 into two parts in more than one way and record each way.
Find the number that goes with a given number to make 10, shown with a drawing or equation.
Add and subtract fluently within 10 (CCSS kindergarten fluency stops at 5).
Solve everyday addition and subtraction story problems within 10 using objects, drawings or equations.
Describe where objects and shapes are using words like above, below, beside, inside, left, right.
Name flat and solid shapes correctly whatever their size or which way they face.
Find flat-shape features, such as faces, on solid objects.
Sort flat and solid shapes and describe how they are alike and different in everyday words.
Build and draw shapes seen in the world with materials like straws or clay.
Directly compare two objects by length, capacity, weight or temperature (temperature is extra).
Understand time ideas like morning, yesterday, week and month, and that clocks and calendars measure time.
Recognize pennies and dimes by name and value.
Collect and sort data into two or three groups and show it with real-object or picture graphs.
Count forward and backward within 120 by ones and tens from any number.
Skip count forward by fives within 120.
Explain what the tens digit and ones digit mean in a two-digit number.
Read, write and show numbers up to 120 with models, words, numerals and expanded form.
Subtract a multiple of 10 from a multiple of 10 (10 to 90) with models and explain.
Find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number in your head.
Compare two two-digit numbers with <, = and > using tens and ones.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths; more equal parts means smaller parts.
Add and subtract within 10 fluently by the end of first grade.
Add and subtract within 20 using objects and a range of strategies.
Use properties of operations, like changing order, to add and subtract within 20.
Add within 100 (two-digit plus one-digit or a multiple of ten) with models; explain the strategy.
Show how addition and subtraction undo each other by solving problems with the inverse operation.
Solve addition and subtraction story problems within 20 of all types, with the unknown anywhere.
Solve story problems that add three whole numbers with a total of 20 or less.
Use the meaning of the equal sign to decide whether addition or subtraction equations are true.
Find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation with three whole numbers.
Tell defining features of shapes from non-defining ones and build or draw shapes with those features.
Put flat or solid shapes together to make a new composite shape.
Measure length by laying copies of a shorter unit end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
Order three objects by length and compare two lengths indirectly using a third object.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog clocks; read digital clocks.
Name pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters and know what each is worth.
Count sets of the same coin (pennies, nickels or dimes) to find totals up to 100 cents.
Organize, show and read data in up to three categories with tallies, picture or bar graphs.
Answer questions about data: total, how many in each category, how many more or fewer.
Count forward and backward within 1,000 by ones, tens and hundreds from any number.
Tell the value of the hundreds, tens and ones digits in a three-digit number.
Read, write and show numbers to 1,000 with models, number names and expanded forms.
Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to or from numbers between 100 and 900.
Compare two three-digit numbers with <, = and > using place values.
Split circles and rectangles into two, three or four equal parts named halves, thirds, fourths.
See that equal parts of the same whole can have different shapes.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently using mental strategies by the end of second grade.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place value, properties or inverse operations.
Add up to four two-digit numbers when the total is 100 or less.
Use a number line to solve addition and subtraction problems within 100.
Use repeated addition to total objects in arrays up to 5 by 5 and write the equation.
Add and subtract within 1,000 using models, drawings or equations.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction story problems within 100 of all types.
Decide if a group of up to 20 is odd or even; write evens as a double.
Identify, describe and draw triangles, pentagons, hexagons and kinds of quadrilaterals.
Describe prisms, cubes and square pyramids by counting their faces, edges and vertices.
Choose a tool, then estimate and measure length to the nearest inch or centimeter.
Measure one object with two units and explain how the numbers relate to unit size.
Measure to find how much longer or shorter one object is than another.
Solve length story problems in one unit using addition and subtraction within 100.
Find the perimeter of polygons in real-world and math problems.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them to find its area.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes on analog clocks, with a.m. and p.m.
Know time relationships: seconds in a minute, minutes in an hour, days, weeks and months in a year.
Solve problems adding and subtracting time intervals in whole or half hours.
Count mixed coins and solve money problems up to 99 cents or whole dollars.
Show data in up to four categories with bar graphs, picture graphs and line plots.
Solve simple put-together, take-apart and compare problems using graph data.
Round four-digit whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100 using place value.
Tell the value of thousands, hundreds, tens and ones digits in a four-digit number.
Read and write numbers up to 10,000 as numerals, in words and in expanded forms.
Compare two four-digit numbers with <, = and > using place values.
Compare two fractions with the same numerator or denominator and justify with models.
See fractions as parts of a whole or of a set (denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, 8).
Split squares, hexagons and triangles into equal parts and name each part as a unit fraction.
Place a unit fraction on a number line.
Place fractions with numerators above 1, including those greater than one, on a number line.
Build a fraction like 3/4 from unit fractions and break it back into a sum of them.
Use number lines and models to find and explain equivalent fractions.
Add and subtract three-digit numbers fluently with place-value strategies and algorithms.
Know multiplication and division facts with factors up to 12 by the end of third grade.
Use commutative, associative and distributive properties as strategies to multiply and divide.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 from 10 to 90.
Find patterns in addition and multiplication tables and explain them with properties.
Solve multiplication and division problems within 100 with equal groups, arrays and both division meanings.
Solve two-step problems with all four operations, writing equations with a letter for the unknown.
Find the missing number in a multiplication or division equation.
Treat division as finding a missing factor.
Understand that quadrilaterals in different groups share features that can define bigger categories.
Spot parallel and perpendicular lines and right angles in shapes and the world around us.
Recognize rhombuses, rectangles and squares as quadrilaterals and draw quadrilaterals that are none of these.
Measure lengths to the nearest half and quarter inch with a ruler.
Describe area as the number of unit squares covering a flat shape with no gaps or overlaps.
Find rectangle area by tiling with unit squares and show it matches multiplying the sides.
Multiply side lengths to find rectangle areas in real-world and math problems.
Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses in standard units.
Solve one-step problems about liquid volume or mass in the same units with any operation.
Tell and write time to the nearest minute on analog clocks.
Solve story problems adding and subtracting time intervals in minutes.
Show data in several categories with scaled picture graphs, scaled bar graphs and line plots.
Solve one- and two-step problems using data in scaled graphs and line plots.
Know a digit is worth ten times what it would be one place to the right.
Read and write numbers up to 1,000,000 as numerals, in words and in expanded forms.
Round five- and six-digit whole numbers to any place.
Compare two five- or six-digit numbers and record with <, = or >.
Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators using common parts or benchmarks like 1/2.
Compare two decimals to hundredths and record with <, = or >.
Break fractions, including mixed numbers and fractions over one, into unit fractions using models.
Explain with models why multiplying top and bottom by the same number gives an equivalent fraction.
Add tenths and hundredths by rewriting the tenths as hundredths.
Write fractions with denominators 10 or 100 as decimals.
Find factor pairs for numbers 1 to 100, sort prime from composite, and spot multiples.
Add and subtract whole numbers up to 1,000,000 fluently, including the standard algorithm.
Multiply four-digit by one-digit numbers and two-digit by two-digit numbers using place value.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit divisors, with or without remainders.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators using models and equations.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number using models and equations.
Solve times-as-many comparison problems and tell them apart from additive comparisons.
Solve multi-step whole-number story problems with all four operations, interpreting remainders.
Solve story problems adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators.
Solve story problems multiplying a fraction by a whole number.
Make a number or shape pattern from a rule and notice features the rule does not state.
Understand angles as two rays from one endpoint, measured in degrees as parts of a circle.
Measure angles in whole degrees with a protractor and draw angles of a given size.
Find unknown angles by adding or subtracting when an angle is split into parts.
Draw and identify points, lines, segments, rays, right, acute and obtuse angles, parallel and perpendicular lines.
Sort triangles and quadrilaterals by parallel or perpendicular sides and angle sizes.
Identify and draw lines of symmetry in flat figures.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles and shapes made of rectangles in real situations.
Convert length, weight and liquid volume from larger to smaller units within one system.
Solve real-world time interval problems that may cross the hour.
Solve money problems with addition and subtraction, including making change.
Solve distance, liquid volume and mass problems, including converting larger units to smaller.
Gather data from observations, surveys or experiments and show it in frequency tables and scaled bar graphs.
Make line plots of fractional measurements and solve like-denominator add and subtract problems from them.
A digit is worth ten times the place to its right and a tenth of the left.
Explain zero and decimal-point patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10; use exponents.
Read and write decimals to thousandths as numerals, in words and in expanded forms.
Round decimals to any place up to thousandths.
Compare two decimals to thousandths by place value and record with <, = or >.
Use models to explain how multiplying by a fraction above or below one changes a whole number.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers fluently, including the standard algorithm.
Divide up to four-digit dividends by two-digit divisors using place value and divisibility rules.
Add and subtract decimals to hundredths with models and place-value strategies.
Multiply and divide decimals to hundredths with models and place-value strategies.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators using common denominators, including word problems.
Understand a fraction a/b as a divided by b and solve problems that way.
Multiply whole numbers by fractions and fractions by fractions, including mixed numbers, with models.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
Solve and write real-world problems that multiply fractions and mixed numbers.
Solve story problems dividing whole numbers where the answer is a fraction or mixed number.
Solve story problems dividing unit fractions by whole numbers and the reverse, using models.
Evaluate expressions with parentheses, brackets and powers of ten using order of operations.
Write simple expressions for calculations and interpret them without working them out.
Make two number patterns from two rules and graph matching terms in the first quadrant.
Classify triangles and quadrilaterals (including kites) in a hierarchy based on their properties.
Find areas of rectangles with fraction or mixed-number sides by tiling and by multiplying.
Measure volume by counting unit cubes in cubic cm, inches, feet or made-up units.
Use the formulas l x w x h or B x h for rectangular prism volume problems.
Find volume of a solid made of two rectangular prisms by adding their volumes.
Convert between units in one measurement system and solve multi-step problems with conversions.
Graph whole-number points in the first quadrant and explain how coordinates match the axes.
Graph points to represent real-world problems and interpret what the coordinates mean.
Gather data and show it in frequency tables, scaled bar graphs and scaled line graphs.
Make line plots of fractional measurements and solve problems using fraction operations on them.

state_code: # SOURCES (Arkansas Mathematics Standards, adopted 2023; DESE page checked 2026-10-01 still lists them as current)

# - Support documents (notes, no CCSS links): K-2 https://docs.google.com/document/d/1b8-w9cQpOSjk6QVMkp7_3umxir5W57qbrNTlCs6B2CE ; 3-5 https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eVi9vE6VxxpZZGtZW3XWr5v641rmbVCu36Ykqz0zUWM
# - No official Arkansas-to-CCSS (or 2016-to-2023) crosswalk was found on the DESE page; every ccss mapping here is my own reading of the text.
# STRANDS (code = grade.STRAND.number; no lettered sub-parts in K-5)
# - NPV = Number & Place Value (clusters: Counting/Counting & Number Foundations, Place Value, Comparison, Fraction Foundations, Equivalent Fractions)
# - CAR = Computation & Algebraic Reasoning (Operations & Properties, Problem Solving, Algebraic Concepts)
# - GM = Geometry & Measurement (Shapes, Measurement Concepts, Length & Width, Perimeter/Area/Volume, Time & Money, Conversions, Coordinate Plane System)
# - Process standards (Standards for Mathematical Practice) are not coded in the K-5 tables and are skipped.
# CCSS K-5 STANDARDS DROPPED OR NOT FOUND
# - K.G.B.6 (compose simple shapes into larger shapes): not in K; composite shapes start at 1.GM.2.
# - 1.OA.C.5 (relate counting to addition/subtraction): no matching standard.
# - 2.NBT.B.9 (explain why add/subtract strategies work): no matching standard.
# - 3.MD.D.8 (perimeter): not in grade 3; perimeter is at 2.GM.7 (polygons) and 4.GM.7 (formulas).
# - 3.NF.A.3c (whole numbers as fractions) is not stated outright (3.NPV.9 has fractions greater than one on a number line).
# - 3.MD.C.7 parts b-d (distributive area models, rectilinear figures) are not spelled out in grade 3; composite rectangles come in 4.GM.7.
# - New: ordinal numbers (K.NPV.3), subitizing (K.NPV.4), time concepts with calendars (K.GM.7), temperature comparison (in K.GM.6), line graphs (5.DA.1).
# - Moved earlier: coins in K and grade 1 (K.GM.8, 1.GM.6, 1.GM.7), skip counting by 5 in grade 1, perimeter and time intervals in grade 2,
#   four-digit place value in grade 3, parallel/perpendicular in grade 3, frequency tables and bar graphs in grade 4 (marked moved from 3.MD.B.3).
# - Fact fluency: K within 10, grade 3 facts to 12 x 12.
# - K.GM.3 (two-dimensional features of solid objects) mapped to K.G.A.3 as edited; it could also be read as new.
# - 2.GM.10 (time unit relationships) mapped to 4.MD.A.1 as moved; days/weeks/months in a year have no CCSS counterpart.
# - 3.NPV.10 (compose/decompose a fraction from unit fractions) listed as edited with 3.NF.A.1 and 4.NF.B.3 because it mixes grade 3 meaning with the grade 4 sum idea.
# - 3.NPV.2-3.NPV.4 (four-digit numbers) mapped to 4.NBT.A.2 as moved: CCSS stops grade 3 place value at 1,000.
# - 2.GM.8 counts squares as "area"; mapped to 2.G.A.2 as edited.
# - kind is judged on content: same = CCSS content with only rewording or small example changes.
